caption: The drawing features a detailed depiction of a metallic object, which appears to be a type of lamp or candlestick, rendered in grayscale pencil or charcoal, giving it a monochromatic appearance of shades ranging from light grey to black. The central object consists of a cylindrical body that widens at the top and is set on a broad, shallow, circular dish or tray, with a handle attached to one side of the cylinder. There is a vertical slit in the cylinder with a small adjustment knob at the base. Above, the cylinder narrows and has a cap-like structure with vent holes around it. In the upper left corner of the drawing, there is a smaller, side-profile sketch of the same object, indicating its proportions and structure. In the upper right corner, a detailed circular close-up shows a grille or a vent, possibly a detail from the upper part of the lamp. The background is plain, with the primary and secondary drawings composed within a single rectangular border. The artist’s signature “Hester Duany” appears in the lower left of the drawing.
title: Lamp
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
